title: Full-support coherent algebra from a finite cover of an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be finite and surjective, and assume $X$ locally Noetherian. Finite means representable and finite on every scheme test [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and surjectivity is on the atlas point spaces [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion, meaning representable and closed on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $Z\prime=Y\times_X Z$ and let $f\prime:Z\prime\to Z$ and $i\prime:Z\prime\to Y$ be its projections. Then $f\prime$ is finite surjective, $i\prime$ is a closed immersion, $Y,Z,Z\prime$ are locally Noetherian, and $G=f\prime_*\mathcal O_{Z\prime}$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module with $\operatorname{Supp}(G)=|Z|$. Modules and quasi-coherence are on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Locally Noetherian means that etale scheme charts are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated (the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests). On a locally Noetherian space, coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. The support of a module is the set of points with nonzero geometric stalk, in the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology].

source.place: Tag 0GF7, lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian, statement and the base-change observations in its proof.

proof.text: Form the sheaf fibre product $Z\prime=Y\times_XZ$. The finite-base-change assertion gives that $f\prime$ is finite. The point-image formula for fibre products gives $\operatorname{im}|f\prime|=|i|^{-1}(\operatorname{im}|f|)=|Z|$, so it is surjective. For any scheme $T\to Y$, $Z\prime\times_YT=Z\times_XT\to T$ is a closed immersion by the assumed scheme-test condition on $i$. Thus $i\prime$ is a closed immersion as well.

source.place: Tag 0GF7 (lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian), proof; scheme-chart expansion of its finite direct-image and unit-section arguments.

proof.text: A closed immersion is finite on scheme tests: over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ its source is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, and the quotient is generated by $1$ as an $A$-module. Now for any finite representable map $H\to B$ with $B$ locally Noetherian, choose a surjective etale atlas of $B$ consisting of Noetherian affine schemes $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its pullback to $H$ is an etale covering by schemes finite over these $U$, hence affine $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C$ finite as an $A$-module. The finite-algebra Noetherian lemma makes each $C$ Noetherian, so these are locally Noetherian etale charts of $H$. Every other etale scheme chart $T\to H$ is then locally Noetherian as well: the family $\{T\times_BU\to T\}$ is a jointly surjective etale covering by schemes, each $T\times_BU=T\times_H\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale, hence locally of finite presentation and so locally of finite type, over the Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and therefore locally Noetherian, and local Noetherianity descends along jointly surjective etale coverings. Thus every etale scheme chart of $H$ is locally Noetherian, as the definition in the statement requires. Apply this first to $Y\to X$ and $Z\to X$, and then to $Z\prime\to Z$. This proves that $Y,Z,Z\prime$ are locally Noetherian; no quasi-compactness of $X$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0GF7 (lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian), proof; scheme-chart expansion of its finite direct-image and unit-section arguments.

proof.text: Fix an etale scheme chart $u:U\to Z$ and put $V=Z\prime\times_ZU$ with $p:V\to U$. Finiteness makes $V$ a scheme and $p$ finite. The ringed-site model identifies etale inverse image with restriction to the localized site. For every etale scheme $W\to U$, both $(G|_U)(W)$ and $(p_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal O_V)(W)$ are $\Gamma(Z\prime\times_ZW,\mathcal O)$: the direct image is precomposition with fibre product. These identities preserve addition, scalar multiplication and restriction, giving $G|_U=p_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal O_V$ as module sheaves. This is an objectwise identity, so no proper or flat base-change theorem is needed.

source.place: Tag 0GF7 (lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian), proof; scheme-chart expansion of its finite direct-image and unit-section arguments.

proof.text: The scheme $U$ is locally Noetherian by step 2, which covers every etale scheme chart of $Z$, and $p$ is finite, so the scheme finite-pushforward theorem applied to $\mathcal O_V$ gives the coherent Zariski module $p_*\mathcal O_V$. The etale/Zariski equivalence compares its associated etale sheaf with $p_{\mathrm{et},*}\mathcal O_V$; its quasi-compact separated hypothesis holds since $p$ is affine: the inverse image of each affine open is affine, and its diagonal on that open is the closed immersion induced by the surjective multiplication map $B\otimes_A B\to B$. Thus the identification in the previous step exhibits $G$ on every etale scheme chart as this coherent module. Quasi-coherence is local for the etale site by its presentation definition, so $G$ is quasi-coherent globally. The chartwise coherence convention in the statement now proves that $G$ is coherent on $Z$.

source.place: Tag 0GF7 (lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian), proof; scheme-chart expansion of its finite direct-image and unit-section arguments.

proof.text: Let $z\in|Z|$, choose a geometric lift in an etale scheme chart $U\to Z$, and restrict $G$ to $U$. Suppose its stalk at that lift is zero. Its unit section $1\in(G|_U)(U)$ then has zero germ. The pointed etale neighbourhood category of this scheme point is cofiltered, and the geometric stalk is its opposite filtered colimit. Zero detection in filtered colimits of additive groups therefore gives a pointed etale neighbourhood $W\to U$ on which the unit section is zero. By step 3, this says $1=0$ in $\Gamma(V_W,\mathcal O_{V_W})$, where $V_W=Z\prime\times_ZW$ is a scheme. Consequently $V_W$ is empty: otherwise taking the germ at any of its scheme points would give $1=0$ in a nonzero local ring. But the fibre-product point-image formula and surjectivity of $f\prime$ imply $V_W\to W$ is surjective, whereas $W$ is nonempty because it has the specified geometric lift. This contradiction proves every geometric stalk of $G$ is nonzero. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}(G)=|Z|$. If $Z$ is empty the equality is vacuous and the earlier steps still apply.
